description: Workbench-reviewed authority/evidence contrast seed batch. Distinguishes authority/status pressure, proof/falsity pressure, provenance pressure, evidence contact, direct support, factual update, and interpretation-layer pressure.

entries.text: The certified source proved the claim false.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The certified source proved the claim false.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence combines source-status pressure with a proof-plus-falsity claim; certification must not substitute for the falsifying evidence chain.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Certification is legitimate only as metadata about process or status; it does not prove the source conclusion.
Proved-false language is legitimate only when the cited evidence directly falsifies the exact claim under the same definitions and scope.

evidence_burden: Identify the evidence being used as proof.
Check whether the evidence falsifies rather than merely weakens the claim.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: separate proof language, falsity closure, and source status; require direct falsifying evidence
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/provenance labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: What exact evidence directly falsifies the exact claim under the same definitions and scope?
What does the certification cover, and is it being substituted for claim-level evidence?

entries.text: An expert said the policy works.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: An expert said the policy works.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence combines expert authority pressure with a policy-effectiveness claim that requires outcome evidence.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Expertise is legitimate prior pressure only when the domain fits the claim and the expert gives inspectable reasons.
A policy-effectiveness claim is legitimate only with a defined outcome, baseline, timeframe, and comparison class.

evidence_burden: Inspect the expert's evidence or reasoning.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: define the outcome metric before accepting effectiveness pressure
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/provenance labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: What outcome metric, baseline, timeframe, and comparison class show that the policy works?

entries.text: There is a consensus, so the debate is over.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: There is a consensus, so the debate is over.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses consensus as authority pressure and converts it into debate-closure pressure.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Consensus is legitimate only when the group, scope, evidence basis, and remaining uncertainty are defined.
Debate-over language is legitimate only when the exact question, evidence basis, and unresolved-question boundary are defined.

evidence_burden: Inspect evidence basis and dissent boundary.
Identify what debate is allegedly over.
Identify the evidence or consensus basis.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: clarify closure/dismissal terms and extract the exact claim
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/provenance labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: What exact debate is being closed, and what unresolved questions remain?

entries.text: The official source posted it, so it is reliable.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The official source posted it, so it is reliable.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence converts official-source provenance into reliability pressure; posting establishes provenance, not truth.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Official status improves provenance but does not make interpretation or conclusion true.
Reliability is legitimate only as source-history pressure; it cannot settle a specific claim without evidence.
Posting or publication establishes provenance of a statement, not truth of the statement.

evidence_burden: Separate the posted content from the content truth.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: treat reliability as source-history pressure, not claim truth
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: treat source/status/provenance labels as metadata or prior pressure, not truth
questions: What source-history evidence supports reliability, and what claim-level evidence supports this claim?
Does posting establish only provenance, or does the post include supporting evidence?

entries.text: The primary document states the deadline was extended.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The primary document states the deadline was extended.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence uses a primary document, a statement relation, and a bounded factual-update claim requiring passage-level scope review.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Primary document contact is legitimate only when the cited passage directly maps to the claim and scope.
A document statement supports a claim only when the exact passage maps to the claim and scope.
A deadline-extension claim is legitimate only when the authority, date, affected case, and scope are identified.

evidence_burden: Check date, authority, scope, and applicability.
Check who had authority to extend it.
Check whether it applies to the relevant case.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: map the document passage to the factual update and check scope
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object directly before support/contradiction movement
questions: Which exact passage states the update, and does it apply to this case?

entries.text: The raw data contradicts the published summary.
entries.literal_meaning: The sentence states or implies: The raw data contradicts the published summary.
entries.candidate_intended_meaning: The sentence pits inspectable raw data against an interpretation-layer summary; contradiction requires method, definition, and scope review.

semantic_operators.legitimacy_condition: Raw-data pressure is legitimate only after definitions, cleaning, exclusions, and method are understood.
Contradiction is legitimate only when record and claim cannot both be true under the same definitions and scope.
A published summary is an interpretation layer and must be checked against the underlying record or raw data.

evidence_burden: Check definitions, dates, scope, and possible reconciliation.
Identify the underlying data or record.
Check whether the summary preserves definitions and scope.

expected_kernel_response.lexical_action: review matched semantic operators and implication-heavy terms
expected_kernel_response.source_trust_action: inspect the evidence object directly before support/contradiction movement
questions: Does the summary preserve the underlying raw data definitions and scope?
What calculation or record in the raw data contradicts the summary?
